samples.comparability: Members measure how much sky is covered, by four incompatible definitions. Opacity-weighted cover (ECCC GEM 'NT') weights each layer by how much light it actually stops, so thin cirrus reads near zero. Geometric cover (GFS, ECMWF, ICON) is a maximum-random overlap of layer fractions and counts thin cirrus in full. A six-hour mean (GEFS) is a time average and is never an instant. Observed dome cover (METAR oktas) is one observer's fraction of the celestial dome at one point. Satellite layered fraction (GOES ABI Cloud Cover Layers) is a retrieval per vertical layer. Values from different definitions must never share a colour ramp, an axis or a difference view.
